#### `vegetation_feature` {#vegetation_feature}

<p class="fl-facts">required · feature identifier · edited on the connection, not in the form</p>

**The feature grown on every column the patch keeps.**

A `namespace:id` that some file in the pack defines. It is placed in the open cell next to the ground the patch just laid -- above it for `floor`, below it for `ceiling` -- never at this feature's own origin, and it runs its own attachment checks there like any other delegate. The reference is resolved once, after the ground layer has already been written, so a file naming a feature nothing defines still lays its whole patch of `ground_block` and simply grows nothing on it; `featurelab check` reports the reference itself, with a near-match suggestion, without running anything. The internal-feature check is different again: when it refuses, the ground layer has been written and the call reports failure anyway.

#### `replaceable_blocks` {#replaceable_blocks}

<p class="fl-facts">required · blockList</p>

**The blocks the patch may dig its ground layer into.**

A column stops filling at the first block that is neither ground_block nor in this list. A column that could not fill even one cell is dropped, so an over-narrow list quietly shrinks the patch.

Must be non-empty.

#### `ground_block` {#ground_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block the patch's ground layer is made of.**

Written downward from the supporting cell, `depth` cells deep.

#### `depth` {#depth}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many cells of ground_block each column lays down.**

Drawn per column from this range. A depth of 0 still keeps the column and still grows vegetation on it -- it just writes no ground.

#### `horizontal_radius` {#horizontal_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How wide the patch is, drawn separately for x and z.**

The patch is wider than this number suggests: each drawn radius is used plus one, so a horizontal_radius of 0 is still a 3x3 patch. The extra outermost ring is the one extra_edge_column_chance gates, and the corners are always trimmed.

#### `vertical_range` {#vertical_range}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number · range [1, −]</p>

**How far a column may search up or down for the ground.**

Used twice: first descending while the cells are open, then climbing back out if that landed inside solid ground. A column that is still buried after that many steps is dropped.

#### `surface` {#surface}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: floor</p>

**Whether the patch grows from the floor or hangs from the ceiling.**

It flips the direction of the search, of the ground fill and of the vegetation together.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `floor` — The patch sits on the ground and its vegetation grows upward. Columns search downward for something that can support the patch, and the ground layer fills downward into it.
- `ceiling` — The patch clings to a ceiling and its vegetation hangs downward. Every direction is mirrored: columns search upward, the ground layer fills upward, and the vegetation grows down.

#### `vegetation_chance` {#vegetation_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · number · absent: 0.0</p>

**Chance to grow the attached feature on any one ground cell.**

Mind the default: 0 means NO vegetation at all -- the patch lays its ground layer and nothing else. Rolled per cell.

#### `extra_deep_block_chance` {#extra_deep_block_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · number · absent: 0.0</p>

**Chance for a column to dig one cell deeper than `depth`.**

Rolled per column, and adds exactly one cell when it hits.

#### `extra_edge_column_chance` {#extra_edge_column_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · number · absent: 0.0</p>

**Chance for a column on the patch's outer ring to be kept.**

Only the single-edge columns are gated -- corners are always dropped and the interior is always kept. At 0 the patch is its interior only, with a clean square edge.

#### `waterlogged` {#waterlogged}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean · absent: false</p>

**Intended to mark the patch as underwater. Avoid it.**

With it on, the patch is walked and its ground blocks are written, and then the collected columns are discarded -- the vegetation never runs and the feature has no defined result to report. The preview reports the placement as failed. Leave it off.
